name: What problems happen if a walk-in shower is not waterproofed correctly?

mainEntity.name: What are the most common signs that a walk-in shower has waterproofing problems after installation?
mainEntity.text: What are the most common signs that a walk-in shower has waterproofing problems after installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Poor waterproofing can cause slow, hidden damage that shows up long after the shower is finished. Early warning signs include grout cracking, tile shifting, musty odors, stains around the base, peeling paint, swelling at nearby trim, and dampness outside the shower area. In more serious cases, the subfloor can soften, the wall board can deteriorate, and mold can develop behind surfaces that look fine from the outside. Because walk-in showers are used daily, even a small leak can spread moisture into surrounding materials over time. That is why waterproofing should be treated as the most important part of the build, not just a technical detail. If a homeowner notices these signs, the shower should be inspected quickly before the damage spreads. A quality installation includes proper substrate prep, sealed corners, careful drain integration, and full membrane coverage in wet zones.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common warning signs include loose tile, grout cracks, soft drywall, mildew smell, water stains, swollen baseboards, and moisture outside the shower area. Waterproofing failures often start small and get worse over time. Once water gets behind the walls or floor, repairs can become expensive and disruptive.
